content.user_title: Build Twilio SMS, Voice, and Verification Workflows
content.value_statement: Communication features require careful handling of credentials, callbacks, compliance, and delivery limits. This skill provides Twilio patterns for SMS, voice IVR, WhatsApp verification, and phone verification.
actual_capabilities: Shows a Python SMS pattern with E.164 validation and status callbacks.
Shows Twilio Verify patterns for 2FA and phone verification.
Shows a TwiML IVR webhook pattern with Twilio signature validation.
Highlights opt-outs, A2P 10DLC, rate limits, and credential handling.
Uses environment variables for Twilio credentials and routing numbers.
limitations: Contains example snippets only; it does not provide a deployable package.
Several code examples are truncated and need completion before use.
Requires a Twilio account, verified sender, credentials, and channel setup.
Does not replace legal review for messaging consent or regional rules.

use_cases.title: Launch Transactional SMS
use_cases.description: Design order updates, alerts, and reminders with delivery callbacks and number validation.

use_cases.title: Add Phone Verification
use_cases.description: Plan signup verification, password reset checks, and 2FA flows with Twilio Verify.

use_cases.title: Create Voice Menus
use_cases.description: Build IVR call routing with TwiML, keypad input, webhook validation, and fallback paths.

prompt_templates.title: Send a Basic SMS
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this Twilio skill to outline a safe SMS notification workflow for [event]. Include credentials, E.164 formatting, and delivery status handling.

prompt_templates.title: Add Phone Verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Twilio Verify flow for [app]. Include signup, resend limits, code checking, error states, and user messaging.

prompt_templates.title: Create an IVR Menu
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a TwiML voice menu for [business]. Include menu options, webhook validation, fallback routing, and logging needs.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Communication Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my planned Twilio implementation for [product]. Check compliance, opt-out handling, rate limits, fraud risks, callback design, and monitoring.

output_examples.input: Design an order shipment SMS flow.
output_examples.output: A concise plan covering E.164 numbers, environment credentials, Twilio client setup, status callbacks, opt-out tracking, and carrier filtering risks.
A verification workflow with send, resend, check, expiration, error states, fraud controls, and user-facing copy points.

output_examples.input: Create a basic support phone menu.
output_examples.output: An IVR outline with greeting text, keypad options, Twilio signature validation, routing destinations, and no-input fallback behavior.

best_practices: Store Twilio credentials in environment variables or a secret manager.
Validate Twilio webhook signatures before processing inbound requests.
Track consent, opt-outs, rate limits, and delivery failures in your application.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode Twilio credentials or phone numbers in source files.
Do not send marketing messages without consent and opt-out handling.
Do not treat example snippets as production-ready without tests and monitoring.

faq.question: Does this skill send messages by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation patterns and prompts for building Twilio features in your own application.

faq.question: Which Twilio services does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers SMS sending, Twilio Verify, TwiML voice IVR, webhook validation, and related operational concerns.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Where should Twilio credentials live?
faq.answer: Use environment variables or a managed secret store. Never hardcode account SIDs, auth tokens, or private routing data.

faq.question: Does it handle compliance requirements?
faq.answer: It highlights consent, opt-outs, A2P 10DLC, and rate limits. You still need legal review for your region.

faq.question: Are the examples production-ready?
faq.answer: No. Some snippets are truncated, and every workflow needs completion, tests, monitoring, and deployment-specific safeguards.
